title: The delegation-of-authority limit, its boundaries and its matrix row are not published, and no source names the rule id or parameter of the approval
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-008); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3.md (A2.8.1, A2.8.3.1, A2.8.3.3); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2.md (T3.2, T6.1, T-A.2); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md (R-UNI-14, R-UNI-15); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R5.5, R9)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 5 and 7; s8 BR2, BR7; s11 Data; s14; CON s3 Preconditions; s11 Data; s12.1, s12.2, s12.8; s14
description: Both legacy criteria require the approval to be inside the delegated limit and to be recorded with its rule version, and both stories therefore need a limit value, its boundaries, the authority-matrix row that carries it and the rule id and version of the step. No read source publishes any of them. The legacy story names FEAT-APD-02 as a dependency and no feature definition of FEAT-APD is in the read extracts. The FSD gives BR-S1-008 (no business value in code, read from reference data with its version) and the roles, and TSD S1 T3.2 gives LOV-APPRAISAL and LOV-ROUTE only. The routing logic names R-UNI-14 (override inside the delegation) and R-UNI-15 (outside the limit) and no rule row, threshold or parameter for the approval. The stories therefore read the limit as governed data with its version, record that version and assert no boundary; the contract declares the element and no value.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-008 story: 'lets the case owner approve the recommended route within their delegated limit' and depends on 'FEAT-APD-02, FEAT-VAL-07'; FSD S1 A2.8.3.1 gives VR-S1-008-1 and BR-S1-008 only and A2.8.3.3 gives the roles; TSD S1 T3.2 lists LOV-APPRAISAL and LOV-ROUTE and no limit; TSD S1 T-A.2 gives the request and response type names and no element; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-UNI-14 and R-UNI-15 give the inside and outside paths with no value.
area: Rules, reference data and authority, S1 rwb-valuation
owner_role: P7 rwb-decision owner with the business owner of module S1 and the owner of the authority matrix
proposed: The authority-matrix owner names the row, its owner and its version, and the rule owner publishes the S1 package; the step then reads the limit with its version and records it, and the contract declares the element with its source and no value.

title: The four consumed rows and the case move publish no operation name, and the plan carries no class C row
source: _work/msr/context/S1.md (ownership rows of S1); Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T-A.1, T5.1, T5.2); Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.8.2); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R5.5)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 4, 5 and 10; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.8 Contract fakes; CON s12.2, s12.8
description: The step reads the case state and answers the case move to rwb-case, reads the rule in force, the authority-matrix limit and the decision-log record from rwb-decision, and authorises through rwb-access, and no source publishes an operation name, a parameter or a transport for any of those rows. The ownership rows of the context pack name three provided S1 operations and no consumed operation. TSD S1 T-A.1 lists only API-S1-001 and T5.1 is the row 'None'. The plan rows for RWB-S1-E4008-APP and -CON carry C as an empty list, so the four rows are built against their documents and fakes on Day 1 and the contract row carries the placeholder.
evidence: The ownership rows of the context pack give S1 three REST operations, no table, no event, no job and one workflow, and name no consumed operation; TSD S1 T-A.1 lists API-S1-001 only; TSD S1 T5.1 is the row 'None'; TSD S1 T5.2 names P3, P7, P4, P5 and P6 as published Java interfaces with no operation; FSD S1 A2.8.2 states the integration point as 'Workbench'; the plan rows for both stories carry C as an empty list.
owner_role: P3 rwb-case owner, P7 rwb-decision owner and P4 rwb-access owner
proposed: The three owners publish their operation names before the wave 3 tag; the clients and their fakes are built from the documented use in the meantime, and a published name is a minor version of the baseline.

title: The element lists of RouteRequest, Approval and the FEAT-VAL-07 recommendation are not published
source: Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T-A.2); Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.7, A2.8.3.2); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (FEAT-VAL-07, FEAT-VAL-08); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-008 Data table)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow step 3; s11 Data; s12.1; CON s4 Flow steps 3 and 4; s11 Data; s12.1; s16
description: TSD S1 T-A.2 names the request and the response types, RouteRequest and Approval, and gives no field table. The legacy Data table lists recovery_case, assignment, decision_log_entry and rule_row with Field IDs, and none of them is an element of the two message types. The FSD A2.8.3.2 field catalog lists the appraisal fields of FEAT-VAL-02 and FEAT-VAL-04, not the route, the reasons, the expected return, the confidence, the alternatives or the limit. The recommendation elements are the output of FEAT-VAL-05 to FEAT-VAL-07 and no source publishes their shape. The stories declare the elements the requirements name (REQ-S1-005 and REQ-S1-006), carry every unknown element with the placeholder, and add no field that a source does not support.
evidence: TSD S1 T-A.2: Request 'RouteRequest', Response 'Approval', no field list; FSD S1 A2.8.3.2 lists v_ace_valuation and valuation_ext fields only; the legacy data row names recovery_case, assignment, decision_log_entry and rule_row; FSD S1 A2.8.4.1 gives the scenario and no message element; no source read for this key gives the type or nullability of a route, a reason, a confidence or a limit element.
owner_role: Contract author, S1, with the platform API owner and the solution architect of S1
proposed: The contract author publishes v1 with the approval elements flat inside Approval, the recommendation carried as a nested element of the same answer, and the unknown types and nullability carried as open P3 items until the first consumer pins the tag.

title: No S1 rule package is in force and no source names the rule id, the rule row or the parameter of the approval step
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.8.3.1 BR-S1-008, A2.8.4.1); Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T3.2, T8); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (Rules sheet); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (FEAT-VAL-08)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s8 BR1, BR5; s9; s13 Configuration and reference data; CON s3 Preconditions; s12.1; s14
description: Both legacy criteria require the result to be written with the rule version, and no S1 route rule id is in force for this feature: the Rules sheet of the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 carries R-UNI-14 and R-UNI-15 for the inside and outside of the delegation but no S1 row for the approval, the S1 package is Phase 2 in the detailed design, and TSD S1 T8 maps every requirement to FEAT-VAL-01. No source names the parameter or the reference-data row that carries the limit either. The story writes whatever rule id and version the decision answer carries into the decision record and never writes a value, a route code or a limit in code.
evidence: FSD S1 A2.8.3.1 gives BR-S1-008 (no business value in code, read from reference data with its version) and A2.8.4.1 states the result is recorded with its rule version; the Rules sheet of the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 carries no S1 row for the approval; TSD S1 T3.2 gives LOV-APPRAISAL and LOV-ROUTE only; TSD S1 T8 maps the requirements to FEAT-VAL-01 and gives no rule id.
area: Rules and reference data, S1 rwb-valuation
owner_role: P7 rwb-decision owner with the business owner of module S1
proposed: The rule owner names the approval rule and its reference-data row and publishes the S1 package, or confirms that the limit stays a governed reference-data row; the record then carries that id and version with no change to the behaviour.
